clue.text: Maybe David's a fortune-teller taking piece of silver

indicators.note: taking means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a palmist tells fortunes by reading the lines of the hand

indicators.note: a piece of the word silver here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A question of whether King David was a soothsayer who accepted a silver coin for his trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe David' signals a definition by example; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms, so he is an example of a psalm writer.

clue.text: Apricots might become this stale over time

indicators.note: might become says the letters of the fruit can be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Fresh fruit left too long might turn dull and dried out.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of APRICOTS equal the answer placed over (above, in a down entry) T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dull and lacking in freshness or imagination, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: An old Mexican's extreme letters seen by sleuth

parts.note: the first and last letters of the alphabet are A and Z
TEC is short for detective

explanation.surface: A historical Mexican figure is spotted by a detective, together with some letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people who ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Cut grass around the top but not the very top of this?

definitions.text: Cut grass around the top but not the very top of this?

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass

indicators.note: but not the very top drops the opening letter of the word for top

parts.note: the head of something is its top

explanation.surface: Mowing the grass of a field but leaving the tips uncut.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a field of grass is what gets cut around its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a field of grass, often cut for hay, which matches the clue's whole picture.

clue.text: Carnivore eats English lamb leaving the head in a vessel

indicators.note: eats means the animal takes the other letters inside itself

parts.note: a stoat is a small flesh-eating mammal

indicators.note: leaving the head drops the first letter of the young sheep

explanation.surface: A meat-eating animal devours English lamb but leaves the head on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' looks like the animal's meal, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat is a ship driven by steam, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: For end of month one ranks KS2 kid

indicators.note: one thing standing for the end of another means it replaces that final letter

parts.note: June is a month of the year
I is the Roman numeral for one
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: At the end of the month, a primary schoolchild is graded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For end of' swaps the last letter of JUNE for I. KS2 is Key Stage 2, the stage of English schooling for ages 7 to 11.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in Key Stage 2 attend junior school in England, so a KS2 kid is a pupil of that age.

clue.text: Ideal uniform jacket to put on a Scotsman

indicators.note: to put on places the earlier pieces above the next in this down entry

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a top is a garment for the upper body, such as a jacket
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A uniform jacket would be the perfect thing for a Scot to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something utopian is perfect or idealised, like the imagined society of More's Utopia.

clue.text: This rota Tim invented holds up copy writers?

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the concealed letters read from bottom to top
holds means the letters sit concealed within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A duty roster that Tim devised is supporting the people who write advertising copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invented' looks like an anagram signal but the letters are simply concealed, backwards, in 'thiS ROTA TIM Invented'. The question mark flags copy writers as people who copy, not advertising copywriters.
explanation.definitionFit: People who copy others are imitators, read here as those who write copies rather than advertising copywriters.

clue.text: See plant grow wild in desert

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters sit within the word for desert

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert them

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of grow run out of order

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a plant that grows wild in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges GROW to GWOR, which goes 'in' RAT. 'See' is a link word directing the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered weed, so it is a type of plant.

clue.text: Scottish child I ejected in a store

indicators.note: ejected means the letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: bairn is the Scots word for a child

explanation.surface: A Scottish child is thrown out of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a farm building used for storing grain or hay, so it is a store.

clue.text: Removed clip and middle of mouth brace after detaching front

indicators.note: the middle of the word mouth is its inner letters
after detaching front means the first letter of the support word is removed

parts.note: a stake braces a plant or post as a support

explanation.surface: A dentist takes off a clip and the brace from the middle of a patient's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes OUT from mOUTh; STAKE less its front gives TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outtake is a piece of film cut from the final version, so a clip that was removed.

clue.text: Paying for a hundred out of every $1000

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
as in 'one in ten', IN expresses a ratio of so many out of every so many
a grand, G, is a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Paying a hundred dollars for every thousand, like a ten per cent fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone for a wrong is to make amends or pay the penalty for it.

clue.text: TV presenter in a late 11th century church?

indicators.note: in means the church abbreviation goes inside the period word

parts.note: the Normans conquered England in 1066 and Norman style marks the late 11th century

explanation.surface: A television host appearing inside an old Norman church.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman churches are typical of England after the 1066 conquest, hence 'late 11th century'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman presents a news programme, linking the reports, so he is a TV presenter.

clue.text: I used to own a small house in this state

parts.note: I'd is a contraction of 'I had', meaning I used to own
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Someone remembers once owning a cottage in a particular American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the north-west of the country.

clue.text: Force group of trees to be cut?

indicators.note: to be cut means the tail of the word is chopped off

parts.note: a copse is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: Someone is forcing a group of trees to be felled.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers collectively make up a force, so the slang for officers stands in for the force.

clue.text: Relative in the navy is under cover in HR

indicators.note: is under means the navy piece sits beneath and inside the cover

parts.note: peel is the outer skin covering fruit

indicators.note: in means the relative goes inside the abbreviation for the navy

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a son is a family relative

explanation.surface: A relative serving in the Navy is working undercover in Human Resources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' is not espionage but the skin of fruit; 'is under' means the navy piece sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: HR, Human Resources, is the department also known by the name for an organisation's staff.

clue.text: Beaten by a rejected crossword clue?

definitions.meaning: a clue from the Down list that has been thrown out or excluded

explanation.surface: Someone is defeated by a crossword clue the editor turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a person defeated and destitute, and humorously a clue that is a Down that is out.

clue.text: Soldier with vehicle going up, round, over — he's on a course

indicators.note: going up in a down entry reads the soldier and vehicle from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: over means the word for round is turned backwards

parts.note: a rota is a round of duties taken in turn

explanation.surface: A soldier in a vehicle goes up, round and over, as if on an obstacle course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns GI+VAN into NAVIG; 'over' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator plots and keeps a ship or aircraft on its course.

clue.text: Keen for prisoner to get transfer for A&E

parts.note: per means for, as in 'per head'

indicators.note: the prisoner is transferred, swapping the letter A for E

parts.note: a captive is a prisoner

explanation.surface: A keen prisoner hopes to be moved to Accident and Emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E, the hospital emergency department, is read as A and E: CAPTIVE with its A changed to E gives CEPTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen can mean sharp or quick in perception, so a perceptive mind is a keen one.

clue.text: Quiet region of Spain — it's superb

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
Aragon is a region of north-eastern Spain

explanation.surface: A quiet Spanish region is said to be excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, something superb of its kind.

clue.text: Revolutionary Marxist caught by wild sex blackmails

indicators.note: caught by means the Marxist is held inside the other letters
wild means the letters of sex are rearranged
revolutionary means turning round, so the Marxist is read backwards

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a type of Marxist

explanation.surface: A revolutionary Marxist caught in a sex scandal resorts to blackmail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reverses TROT to TORT, 'caught by' EXS, from 'wild' rearranging SEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Extorts means obtains by threats or force, which is what blackmail does.

clue.text: Accustomed to American education

explanation.surface: Someone has become comfortable with the American way of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: To be familiar with something, as in 'got ___ to it', means to be accustomed.

clue.text: With concentration, studies depend on ignoring the principal

parts.note: a den is a private study room

indicators.note: ignoring the principal drops the first, leading letter

parts.note: to rely is to depend

explanation.surface: Students in their studies depend on the head teacher not noticing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' means first or chief, so RELY loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Densely means thickly packed, with a high concentration of things in a space.

clue.text: Die? Three couples found In God We Trust

indicators.note: three pairs of letters are found within the motto, with the rest discarded

explanation.surface: A question about death answered by the motto on American banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pick three pairs from the motto: GO from God, WE, and ST from the end of Trust. The question mark marks a euphemism; the phrase also recalls 'Go West, young man'.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off into the sunset is a slang euphemism for dying, so the phrase can mean die.

clue.text: Maybe base of tree as time moves on is a place to rest

indicators.note: moves on means the letter shifts further along the word

parts.note: roots are found at the base of a tree

explanation.surface: A tree's base, as time passes, becomes a place to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves on' shifts T one place along ROOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds settle to sleep, so it is a resting place.

clue.text: Ban on golf supplanting an unknown marsh plant

indicators.note: supplanting means the second letter takes the place of the first

parts.note: a boycott is a ban on dealing with someone
Y is an unknown in algebra
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ban on golf replaces something nobody knew about.
explanation.walkthrough: In BOYCOTT, G 'supplanting' Y gives BOGCOTT, then ON.
explanation.definitionFit: This sedge with white cottony heads grows in boggy ground, so it is a marsh plant.

clue.text: Liberal is up before Liberal beak

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: One Liberal politician rises before another and makes a pronouncement.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's beak is also called its bill, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bone fragment turning up on outskirts of Ithaca

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry reads the fragment from bottom to top

parts.note: a bit is a fragment

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A fragment of bone turns up on the edge of a Greek island town.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger bone of the lower leg.

clue.text: Demolish large new English comprehensive

indicators.note: demolish means the letters are knocked down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An order to knock down a big new English secondary school.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'comprehensive' is a British state secondary school, misleading the reader from the adjective meaning all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean wide-ranging or not limited to particulars, as in a broad overview.

clue.text: Highest part including top of mountain in quake

indicators.note: including means the top letter goes inside the musical part

parts.note: the treble is the highest part in music

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The summit of a mountain is caught up in an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: To quake is to shake or shiver, which is a synonym for the answer as a verb.

clue.text: The smallest expression of admiration?

parts.note: an exclamation used to show one is impressed, read literally as meaning not any smaller amount

explanation.surface: The most minimal way of showing that you admire something.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is said in admiration, as in 'a duke, ___!', but literally says the amount cannot be smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation expresses being impressed, and its words literally mean nothing smaller.

clue.text: Part of France — is it like the UK say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is only spoken like the region's name

parts.note: Britain plus the suffix -y gives a jokey word meaning resembling Britain

explanation.surface: A question of whether a French region resembles Great Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The name means 'little Britain', settled by Britons, so the joke is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: This region in north-west France is a peninsula with Celtic roots, one of the country's historic provinces.
